scope: Proposition 10.1 (Confined crossings) of the manuscript “Uniform marked-polygon estimates and sharp finite bridge moments” (preprints/Uniform-marked-polygon-estimates-and-sharp-finite-bridge-moments-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e9b7a0252f329287), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 99-100. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following statements hold with constants depending only on the fixed relative tolerances and pure normals. • Starting at a midpoint with inward normal n, one can travel in that half-plane to a pure terminal line at distance s from the source whose outward normal m differs from n by at most 60◦, staying before the terminal line until crossing at the end. For any fixed positive relative tolerance, and all sufficiently large admissible s with a threshold depending only on that tolerance, the travel can be confined within that tolerance around the straight segment in direction m, with mass ≳ s−1/4. Also the unrestricted mass in this two-cut domain is O(s−1/4). • From one specified midpoint to another on the same pure boundary at distance l > 0, one can use half-plane arches of diameter O(l) with mass ≳ l−5/4; even without confinement the mass is O(l−5/4). 99 The boundary-to-boundary mass is also decreasing as the terminal port moves away from the source along one straight side of a convex pure-sided truncation, whenever the compared adjacent ports remain on that side.
